summary: The tree's KO- is wrong. The leaf is S[KO+], the checker's label. Black must take at A18 at once (otherwise White's C19 captures B19 and lives with eyes at A18 and B19), and each capture threatens at once. White has no local threat: against White's F19 or A15, Black simply connects at A19, gives up three stones, plays the vital point A19 again, and White is left with one eye. It is not a bent four either, since White can retake and live at C19. This reads the outside as Black's, as the tree's own blocks at G18-J18 do; the wider area's searches stay undecided.
variations:
1. A18 A15 A19 C19 A19 A18 F19: White's best try A15 is no threat. Black connects (giving up A18, A19 and B19), White captures at C19, Black's A19 takes the vital point, and after F19 White has one eye at most. Black wins with equal threats (solver continues C15 A14 B14 D15 B19 B15 pass A19).
2. A18 F19 A19 C19 A19 G18 H18 A18 G17 B19 G19: capturing E19 is no threat either. Black ignores it. G17 and H18 surround G18, G19 takes it, and F19 is left in atari at E19. White keeps only the corner eye, and Black wins (solver: White to move there, Black wins; after G18, Black wins at s=o=0).
3. A18 A19! pass C19: with one threat more, White retakes and lives (Black fails at s=0, o=1).
4. pass C19: if Black does not take, White captures B19 and lives.
5. A18 pass A19 ...: with White passing once, Black kills even against four White threats, so Black's capture is direct.
6. A18 A19! A15 C19: the bent-four rule's line. White lives when it may retake, so the rule does not kill.
